content.value_statement: Complex React flows often fail through missed awaits, hidden transitions, and weak error states. This skill guides explicit state design, validation, UI feedback, and integration tests.
actual_capabilities: Maps multi-step React operations into explicit states and transitions.
Defines preconditions, actions, postconditions, and error handling for each step.
Shows async flow implementation patterns with validation and contextual logging.
Models UI-facing flow state for loading, complete, and error screens.
Guides integration tests for happy paths and failure cases.
Explains when to consider XState for more complex state machines.
limitations: It provides patterns and examples, not a complete state machine library.
It does not generate production-ready payment or checkout integrations.
It assumes React or React Native project knowledge.
It does not replace security or compliance review for transactional flows.

use_cases.title: Implement Checkout Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan validation, payment, confirmation, and recovery states before writing React flow logic.

use_cases.title: Debug Async Ordering Bugs
use_cases.description: Trace missed awaits, invalid transitions, and weak postconditions in existing multi-step flows.

use_cases.title: Document Team Flow Decisions
use_cases.description: Create shared flow diagrams, transition rules, and test expectations for complex product journeys.

prompt_templates.title: Map A Simple Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new feature flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use react-state-flows to map my React flow into states, transitions, preconditions, postconditions, and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Hidden Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup for scattered async logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-step React operation and suggest an explicit flow structure with validation after each step.

prompt_templates.title: Add UI Flow State
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced state modeling for user feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design UI-facing flow states for loading, success, retry, and error handling in this React Native workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Flow Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my integration test plan for this React flow and identify missing happy path and failure path coverage.

output_examples.input: A checkout feature has validation, payment, and confirmation steps.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a state sequence, transition rules, postcondition checks, error states, and integration test targets.

output_examples.input: A React Native onboarding flow fails when users retry after an API error.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies retry states, failed step context, UI status needs, and recovery test cases.

output_examples.input: A team needs to decide whether to adopt XState.
output_examples.output: The skill compares current flow complexity against XState triggers such as branching, shared machines, and visualization needs.

best_practices: Document each state before implementing flow logic.
Validate postconditions after every async step.
Test happy paths and failures at each step.
anti_patterns: Do not hide ordering inside scattered callbacks.
Do not update UI status without recording the active step.
Do not rely only on unit tests for full flow behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill require XState?
faq.answer: No. It explains explicit flow patterns first and suggests XState only for more complex cases.

faq.question: Can it help with React Native?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to React web and React Native flows with async steps.

faq.question: What state libraries does it assume?
faq.answer: The examples use Zustand style stores, but the patterns apply to other React state tools.

faq.question: Can it design error handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes error states, failed step context, retries, and user feedback.

faq.question: Does it create production checkout code?
faq.answer: No. It provides flow structure guidance and examples, not payment provider integration.

faq.question: How should teams use it?
faq.answer: Use it before implementation, during refactors, and when reviewing integration test coverage.
